reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown close the tenfold gap by reading Kings' term for stall as covering ten horses per unit, matching Chronicles' single-horse stalls.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses the ten Kings and four Chronicles thousand-stall totals as a flat factor-of-ten discrepancy about the same king's stables.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
sides.verseText: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.

sides.snippet: Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
sides.verseText: Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
